name: USS Iowa

propulsion._speedNote: 33 knots was the design figure and was exceeded on trials at light displacement; 32.5 is often quoted for full load. 33 is used here as the deep-load design speed.

manoeuvring._turningNote: Twin rudders gave the Iowas a notably tight circle for their length: about 814 yards tactical diameter at 30 knots, which is roughly 2.75 lengths. Rounded to 3.0 to sit between the light and deep-load trial figures.

sources: US Navy Bureau of Ships booklet of general plans, BB-61 (1943)
Friedman, US Battleships: An Illustrated Design History (1985)
NavWeaps: USA 16"/50 Mark 7 and Iowa-class particulars

confidence.maxSpeedKn: medium — sources give 32.5 to 33 knots depending on load and trial conditions
confidence.tacticalDiameterLengths: medium — trial figures vary with speed and load

notes: Fast battleship: her 33 knots came from a hull 20 m longer than a South Dakota's for the same armour scheme, which is why she is so much finer forward.
